typescript.apps/desktop/electron/main/bootstrap/win: Existing window lifecycle extraction from the main-process facade; further decomposition is outside this follow-up scope.
typescript.packages/agent-runtime/src/native-pi-ses: Native Pi continuation regression coverage is kept with the source boundary while the protocol and fixture contract stabilise; split by lifecycle once the native adapter surface settles.

Native Pi discovery, immutable projection, guarded continuation, and fork publication share one sidecar-private source boundary; split by lifecycle once the native adapter contract stabilises without widening path ownership.
Host-side fan-out broker: it owns source registry resolution, per-source deadline and cancellation, child-call dispatch through tools.execute, and outcome normalisation. Those concerns share one dispatch lifecycle because the deadline clock, the in-flight permit, and the outcome it produces must be decided at the same point; splitting them would separate the decision from the evidence that justifies it. The source descriptor table and aggregation already live in trial-sources.ts and trial-orchestrator.ts, so this file is the dispatch boundary only and will be split once a second composite tool needs the same broker.
typescript.apps/desktop/electron/main/trial-orchest: Host-side aggregation for the unified trial query: it owns per-source verdict rendering, coverage and lower-bound disclosure sentences, record tagging, deduplication, and the manual-overlap warning. These are deliberately colocated because every one of them is a disclosure the user reads as one paragraph, and the audits that produced them each found the same defect class - a sentence asserting a reason the data did not support. Keeping the sentences next to the code that decides which reason applies is what makes that class of defect reviewable; the source registry and the fan-out broker are already separate files. Will be split by disclosure group once the WHO ICTRP attribution surface stops changing.
